scenes.heading: Managing equipment, supplies, and vehicle costs

sents.d: Managing equipment, supplies, and vehicle costs
Underestimating these costs is a common reason margins run thinner than expected.
Equipment, supplies, and vehicle expenses (fuel, maintenance, wear and tear) are easy to underestimate when first pricing jobs, and can quietly erode margins that looked healthy on paper.
Tracking these costs specifically — not just lumping them into general business expenses — makes it possible to see whether current pricing actually covers them with a reasonable margin left over.
Building a simple reorder system for consumable supplies, rather than realizing you're out mid-job, prevents both wasted time and the unprofessional appearance of an unprepared visit.

take: Track equipment, supplies and vehicle costs so pricing covers them.
